newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: COSTA RICA ORDERS THREE GOLD MINE CLOSURES.
newsitem.headline: COSTA RICA ORDERS THREE GOLD MINE CLOSURES.

text.p: Costa Rica on Thursday ordered the closure of three gold mines in the Guanacaste province, party due to environmental concerns, the Environment and Energy Minister said.

Rene Castro told a media conference that Minas de Sierra Alta and Abece Griego, both with majority Canadian investment capital, and an unnamed mine which is a project of the National Union of Miners, had been closed down. He did not specify which Canadian companies were involved.
"The closures have been ordered because the mines do not comply with the basic requisites of being economically viable, of producing social benefits and of not damaging the environment," Castro said.

Castro added the closure of Minas de Sierra Alta and Abece Griego were permanent, although open to appeal, and the National Union of Miners project was for 90 days to give the group time to put their house in order.

Sierra Alta, he said, had been operating with losses and from a governmental point of view did not justify being operated. Among other anomalies, open pit mining had been undertaken there without authorization, he added.
At Abece Griego, he added, there was a lack of topographic control and an inspection had revealed uncharted tunnels in operation.
In the union's project, Castro said uncharted tunnels were also found and that mine waste had been dumped causing a pollution hazard to the province's Boston river.
